solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Explode main target or lose it

parts.note: a bomb that explodes is said to go off
the main is an old poetic name for the sea, also called the deep
a target is an aim or goal, an end in view

explanation.surface: A demolition order: blow up the main target, or else lose your nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose it' here is slang for losing one's temper or self-control, not for missing the target.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for suddenly losing one's temper or composure.

clue.text: Sense morgue's developed?

indicators.note: letters that have developed have grown into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what feeling a mortuary gives you.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram of SENSE MORGUES and a description: the feeling a morgue produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A morgue full of corpses produces a sense of horror and ghastliness.

clue.text: Lithe swimmer that might be more excessive?

definitions.meaning: a sleek river mammal that swims
OTT means over the top, excessive, so a jokey comparative ... would mean more excessive

explanation.surface: A sleek swimmer who may be overdoing things.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, short for 'over the top', is British slang for excessive; adding -ER makes a mock comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: The river mammal is famously lithe in water; the second sense is a pun on OTT plus a comparative ending.

clue.text: Most liked involving London School of Economics, an instant unwise action

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the favourite word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a fave is a favourite, the most liked
a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: A favourite student at a famous London university does something rash in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most liked' gives the informal word for a favourite; 'involving' means the two later pieces sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistaken step or blunder is an unwise action.

clue.text: Present jerk as a contrarian

parts.note: to be present is to be here
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: Someone presenting a fool as a contrary thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' and 'jerk' look like a verb and its object but are two adjoining synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dissents from accepted doctrine is a contrarian of a sort.

clue.text: Weaken Mediterranean island faction, briefly on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on the rise means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a side is a faction or party

explanation.surface: A rising party on a Mediterranean island weakening the regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts SIDE to SID; 'on the rise' turns ELBASID upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To incapacitate something is to weaken or cripple it.

clue.text: Dismiss Parisian I found in European Court

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the French pronoun sits within the court letters

parts.note: E for European plus CT, the abbreviation for court
je is French for I, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is thrown out after being found in a European court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals a French word; 'found in' places it within the court abbreviation, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out or expel someone is to dismiss them.

clue.text: Radical heading taken from short message about veil?

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a text is a short message sent by phone
re means about or concerning
mist is a veil over the landscape

explanation.surface: A radical's text about wearing a veil, with its heading removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading taken from' strips the first T from TEXT, leaving EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical is a person holding extreme views.

clue.text: When bird's taken off jauntily, what one gets up to

indicators.note: taken off means removed, so the bird's letters are stripped out of the word

parts.note: the jay is a noisy bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bird takes off jauntily, and one wonders what it gets up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jauntily' looks like an adverb for the flight but is the word itself; remove J, A and Y from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to and the answer are synonyms marking a limit in time or extent.

clue.text: One of three poetic siblings sets trio off

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A poet among siblings sets three people off.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante Gabriel, Christina and William Michael were the three Victorian siblings who wrote poetry; there was also a fourth sibling, Maria.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina and Dante Gabriel of that surname were both poets, as was William Michael.

clue.text: Buckled under, skirting main point, before being off the record

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge of, so the jumbled letters enclose the rest
buckled means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the gist is the main point
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone collapsing under pressure, avoiding the main point, before going off the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckled' rearranges the fodder to UNRED, and 'skirting' wraps that around the other two pieces, leaving only the final D after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not entered in any official list is off the record.

clue.text: Early wind instrument exhibit has a majority brought back

indicators.note: a majority is more than half, and brought back means turned round, so the first four of seven letters are reversed

parts.note: to exhibit is to present

explanation.surface: A museum display of an old wind instrument, mostly returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a majority brought back' reverses PRES, the first four letters of seven, to SERP, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaking bass wind instrument of the Renaissance, early ancestor of the tuba.

clue.text: Flanked by my team, brought in to have lasted a decade?

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so the team pronoun goes into the middle

parts.note: to be ten is to have lasted a decade
we is what you call yourself and your team

explanation.surface: A long-serving player surrounded by the team has been there ten years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have lasted a decade' is BE TEN; 'brought in' places WE inside it after BE T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flanked on both sides sits in the middle, which is the preposition's sense.

clue.text: Meyerhof's forename written on his initial device

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: the initial of Meyerhof is M
Otto Meyerhof was a German biochemist and Nobel laureate

explanation.surface: A scientist's first name inscribed on his monogram.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto Meyerhof won the 1922 Nobel Prize for work on muscle metabolism.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a device is an emblem with a phrase or maxim, the sense of a guiding saying.

clue.text: Film-maker is to smear opposite number

parts.note: to tar is to smear, as in tar someone's reputation
anti means opposed or opposite

explanation.surface: A director accused of smearing his rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite number' looks like one phrase meaning a counterpart, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin of that surname is the American director of Pulp Fiction.

clue.text: Old Street Church holds masses with papers

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the church letters wrap the rest

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
heaps means masses, lots
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: An old church on Old Street hosting masses and newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Street' looks like the London road of that name; it is the definition, a historic City of London street that was a medieval market.
explanation.definitionFit: A City of London thoroughfare dating back to the medieval market, so an old street.

clue.text: Soft drug support occupies one holding the strings?

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: occupies means fills the inside of, so the support goes inside the drug

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A soft drug's supplier controlling the user like strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupies' puts the golf support inside the drug, just before its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette operator works the strings, which the question mark flags as literal rather than figurative control.

clue.text: Entitled women manage in turn to keep one tender

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the letter for one is held within
in turn means turned round, so the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: dames are women holding a title
to run is to manage
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Titled ladies take turns managing to keep a carer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reverses DAMESRUN to NURSEMAD; 'to keep' puts I in before the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is someone who looks after others, as a children's carer does.

clue.text: Native American father stops ascent of character in Gone With the Wind

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the father goes inside
in a down clue an ascent reads upwards, so the name is reversed

parts.words: character in Gone With the Wind
parts.note: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine of Gone With the Wind
pa is father

explanation.surface: A father halts the rise of a character in a classic Civil War novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascent of' reads Scarlett's surname upwards to give ARAHO; 'stops' plugs father into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of the Great Plains, so a Native American nation.

clue.text: After an operation, take down one's particulars (suggestively?)

definitions.text: After an operation, take down one's particulars (suggestively?)

parts.words: After an operation, take down one's particulars (suggestively?)
parts.note: officially, questioning someone after a mission; suggestively, removing their underpants, the briefs

explanation.surface: Collecting someone's details after a mission, or something racier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particulars' are details, but 'take down' also means remove, and briefs are underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Questioning someone after a mission or operation for a report, with a saucy hint at removing underwear.

clue.text: Man with a signature dish of stewed tripe

indicators.note: stewed means cooked up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A chef famous for his signature stewed tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'signature dish' suggests a chef, but the dish is the laboratory one named after its inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Richard of that surname, German bacteriologist, gave his name to the culture dish.

clue.text: Vocal artist's misbehaviour directed towards Royal Academy

parts.note: a sin is misbehaviour
at means aimed or directed towards
RA is the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A singer's scandalous behaviour aimed at the art establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank of that surname was a celebrated singer, a vocal artist.

clue.text: Precious time needed for throwaway message?

parts.note: twee means precious, affectedly dainty

explanation.surface: Is valuable time needed for a disposable note?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' means valuable on the surface but here is the affected sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A post on the social platform X is a short, quickly forgotten message.

clue.text: Protecting Queen Mother, laid something under a pint?

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the wager wraps the royal pieces

parts.note: to have laid a wager is to have bet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on the Queen Mother while sipping a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid' looks like 'put down' but it is the gambling sense: laid a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard coaster placed under a pint glass in a pub.

clue.text: Mother wraps good, hot filling in crust

indicators.note: wraps means encloses, so the mother word goes round the letter

parts.note: mama is mother

explanation.surface: Mum wraps up a good hot pie filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crust' suggests pastry; it is the Earth's crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock lies beneath and within the Earth's crust, a hot filling.

clue.text: Low-calorie allowance's lost on educated set

parts.note: lite is the marketing spelling for low-calorie

indicators.note: lost means removed, so the two letters drop out

parts.note: a ration is an allowance

explanation.surface: A dieter's allowance is wasted on the well-educated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost on' looks like 'not appreciated by'; 'lost' takes ON out of RATION, leaving RATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned, literary people form an educated set.

clue.text: Keen to risk reversing direction at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset means the first letter, and reversing direction swaps west for east

parts.note: to wager is to risk money

explanation.surface: Someone keen to gamble on turning round from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: W (west) at the start of WAGER becomes E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen means being enthusiastic and impatient to do something.

clue.text: National Trust dispute in aid of blocking perverse old person in scrum

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, inside the other word

parts.note: froward is an old word for perverse
NT is the National Trust
a row is a dispute
for means in aid of, as in collecting for charity

explanation.surface: A heritage charity row over a fund-raiser held up by a stubborn old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' sets the three middle pieces inside the archaic word, split after FRO. The National Trust is a British heritage charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop or hooker in rugby packs down in the front of the scrum.
